recognize_zh: 視野中央與左下各有一個比紅血球還大、無核、帶紫色顆粒與淡藍邊緣的結構，對照旁邊的嗜中性球與一般小血小板，可認出是巨大血小板（giant platelets）。
features: Two anucleate platelets clearly larger than adjacent red cells (giant platelets), one central and one at lower left
Central giant platelet with a dense purple granular center and a pale blue, irregular peripheral hyalomere
Lower-left giant platelet with flattened, finely granular lilac cytoplasm and angular outline
Other scattered platelets are small, providing internal size comparison
Two segmented neutrophils and, at the left edge, a partially visible granulocyte with coarse purple granules; thick area with crowded red cells
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear, in a relatively thick area with crowded red cells, shows two platelets that exceed the diameter of adjacent red cells. The central platelet has a compact purple granulomere with a pale blue fringed rim, and the lower-left platelet is flattened with fine lilac granules. Other platelets are small, and two segmented neutrophils are present; a coarsely granulated granulocyte is partly visible at the left edge. Findings are consistent with giant platelets, which may reflect increased platelet turnover, a myeloid neoplasm or an inherited macrothrombocytopenia; correlation with platelet count and history is required.

ddx.vs: A lymphocyte has a dense nucleus with a rim of blue cytoplasm, whereas giant platelets are anucleate with granular purple centers.
Micromegakaryocytes contain a dense, often lobulated nucleus, which is absent in these platelets.
A clump is composed of multiple discrete platelets with separate granulomeres, rather than a single large platelet with one continuous outline.
